title: Mound: a ring round the door, or a crescent on the side away from the food?
question: Which mound do you want the teacher to aim for: ring (left) or crescent (right)?
context_md:
Same harvester nest (7-cell chambers), same soil, heaped two ways. Top row: sized for 12 ants (the planned colony stage). Bottom row: the full stack. Food 45 columns east; the yellow dots are the walk from the door to it.

- **In a 2D slice the mound holds all the soil the nest took out.** Nothing spreads into a third dimension, so the mound's area equals the nest's.
- **A ring puts a hill on every trip to the food.** The trip climbs 8-11 rows. In the old game the ants tunnelled through it instead, and blocking those tunnels starved the colony (dead-ends `MOUND_DIG`, `FORAGER_NODIG`). The mound arm was also the worst at keeping the door open: 30 of 72 samples against 54.
- **A crescent leaves the road flat, but is twice as long or taller on one side.** Real ants build both shapes: a ring in Dorymyrmex; a one-sided crescent in Trachymyrmex and Pheidole, turned away from the slope.
- **Middle ground:** a lopsided ring, mostly on the far side with a thin one on the food side.

items.label: ring vs crescent
items.caption: left: ring, right: crescent; top: 12-ant nest, bottom: full harvester
